title: Strange Printer
summary: Determine the least number of print cycles required for a printer that can only print identical characters in a sequence and can overwrite any part of the string at once, given a string s.
statement: Determine the least number of print cycles required for a printer that can only print identical characters in a sequence and can overwrite any part of the string at once, given a string s.
constraints: 1 <= len(s) <= 100; the string contains lowercase letters.
One turn prints one repeated character over any contiguous interval and may overwrite earlier characters.
hints: Equal characters printed in one turn can cover material that is overwritten later.
Use interval DP and merge the first character’s turn with a later equal character.
Start with 1+dp[left+1][right]; for each equal s[k], try dp[left+1][k-1]+dp[k][right].
The final visible copy at the left endpoint either has its own turn or shares the turn producing a later equal endpoint.
editorial: The final visible copy at the left endpoint either has its own turn or shares the turn producing a later equal endpoint.

tests.explanation: Print all a characters in one turn and all b characters in a second turn.
Print aaa, then overwrite the middle with b, using two turns.
